title: White Label Client Portal: What It Is & Best Platforms
summary: White Label Client Portal: What It Is & Best Platforms
body_markdown:
A client logs in to check on their project and lands on a page with another company's logo, a URL they don't recognize, and a menu that has nothing to do with the work you do for them. So they email you instead.


A white label client portal fixes that: clients log in on your domain, under your brand, and find what they need without asking. But branding is the easy part; the harder questions are whether you can control exactly what each client sees, and whether your team can run the work behind the portal in the same place. This guide compares five platforms on all three.


## **TL;DR**


A white label client portal is a secure online space that carries your own branding, where clients log in to see the files, updates, reports, or tasks that matter to them, without digging through email or a dozen different tools.


- A white label client portal is a secure website where clients log in under your brand, on your domain, to see their files, project status and invoices. **‍**
- AI has changed the build question. It's no longer "AI or no AI", but whether the AI writes code you then have to maintain, or builds your portal on a platform that already handles logins, permissions, and hosting.
- Judge platforms on three jobs, not just branding: how fully you can brand the portal, how tightly you control what each client sees, and wether your team can manage the work behind it in the same system.
- Five options compared: Assembly, Softr, Zite, SuiteDash, and Noloco. They differ on fixed workflows, AI-generated apps, all-in-one suites, and building around your existing data.
- Client coordination work quietly costs real money: a 2026 survey found firms lose a median of $60,000 a year to it, chasing documents, answering "can you send that again," and tracking who's waiting on what ([Progress Software, State of Client Collaboration 2026](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/07/30/3336122/0/en/Professional-Services-Firms-Lose-60K-a-Year-to-Inefficient-Client-Coordination-New-Progress-Software-Report-Finds.html) ).


## What is a white label client portal?


A white label client portal is a secure online space where your clients log in under your business' branding, not the software provider's. "White label" means the vendor's name is removed from everything the client sees: the login page, the web address, the emails they receive, and any "powered by" badge.


Inside the portal, clients can typically:


- Check the status of their project
- Access files and deliverables
- Complete onboarding forms
- Approve work before it moves forward
- View reports built from their own data
- Upload documents you're waiting on
- See invoices or account information


The hard part is keeping this consistent across every client, without a developer rebuilding the portal each time your process changes.


## Why use a white label portal?


Because chasing clients is slow, unpaid work - simple! In the[State of Client Collaboration 2026 survey](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/07/30/3336122/0/en/Professional-Services-Firms-Lose-60K-a-Year-to-Inefficient-Client-Coordination-New-Progress-Software-Report-Finds.html) by Progress Software (the company behind ShareFile), firms in accounting, law, financial services and healthcare said they spend nearly 20 hours a week collecting documents and signatures, following up, clarifying requests and tracking tasks. At $65 an hour, that's a median of roughly $60,000.


A portal doesn't eliminate client coordination, but it moves that back-and-forth into one place:


- **Give clients one place to find everything.** Project updates, files, reports, forms, and requests live in one login instead of five different tools.
- **Show each client only the information they need.** One client sees their project. They don't see anyone else's.
- **Reduce "can you send that again" emails.** If it's already in the portal, they can go find it themselves.
- **Let clients check progress without asking your team.** Fewer status-check emails means fewer interruptions.
- **Make your service feel like your own product.** Your logo, your domain, your colors, no trace of the software underneath.
- **Keep sensitive client information separate and secure.** One client's data isn't visible to another, even inside the same portal.

## What features should a white label client portal have?


Most portals need to cover the same ground: security, permissions, integrations, reporting, file handling, forms, workflow automation, and branding. A few of these are worth more scrutiny than others.


To compare them properly, group the features by the three jobs the portal has to do:


**1. Look like your business**


- Your own domain, such as portal.yourcompany.com
- Your logo, colors, and fonts on every page, including the login screen
- Emails (invites, password resets, notifications) sent with your branding
- No vendor logo or "powered by" badge anywhere clients can see it
- A portal that works on a phone, since clients often check in on the go


**2. Control what each client sees**


- Role-based access, so your team, partners and clients each see a different slice of the system
- Record-level permissions, so two clients can share the same portal and never see each other's data
- The option to hide internal fields, like notes or rates, from clients
- Easy client login, such as single sign-on
- Audit logs swhoing who accessed what


**3. Run the work behind the portal**


- A data layer you control, such as your existing database, spreadsheets, or CRM
- A view for your team across every client's work, not just the client-facing pages
- Automations that run on client actions, like moving a job forward when a client approves it


## How do you choose a white label client portal platform


Ask these questions of every platform you're considering before you commit to it:


1. **Can you connect the tools and data you already use?** Check whether you can point it at your existing CRM, database, or spreadsheets, rather than copying everything into a new system.
2. **Can each client see only their own information?** Confirm you can control access by client, company, role, or project, not just by a single shared login.
3. **Can the portal match how your team actually works, including the exceptions?** You should be able to build pages around your real onboarding, delivery, and approval process, not force your process to match the tool's template.
4. **Can you brand the whole experience? And which plan removes the vendors's branding?** Custom domain, logo, colors, and emails, with no visible trace of the software provider.
5. **Can different clients get different experiences?** One client might need project reports, another just onboarding tasks and documents.
6. **Will your team need a developer to maintain it?** If every small change requires engineering time, the portal falls behind your business fast.
7. **How does pricing change as you add clients?** This matters more for service businesses adding external users regularly than it does for internal-only tools.
8. **Can your team manage the work behind the portal in the same system** , or will someone copy updates across from a spreadsheet?


The last question is the one most buyers skip. If the portal and your team's workspace use different data, someone has to keep them in sync by hand, and clients end up seeing stale information.


## How do off-the-shelf portals, custom builds, and AI portal builders compare?


AI means you no longer need a development team to get a portal built. What matters now is where the AI's work ends up. There are three routes:


- **Off-the-shelf portal software** . Quick to set up, but you work inside the vendor's template.
- **Custom code** , written by developers or generated by an AI coding tool. It fits exactly, but you own the code: hosting, logins, permissions, security fixes, and every change after launch.
- **An AI portal builder.** You describe the portal and AI builds it on a platform that already handles logins, permissions, hosting, and branding. What the AI builds shows up as pages, data, and access rules you can check and change without reading code.


Off-the-shelf portal software Custom code (developers or AI coding tools) AI portal builder (Noloco)


**How you get the first version** Set up the vendor's template Developers write it, or an AI tool generates the code from a prompt Describe it to[Nola](https://noloco.io/product/nola) , which builds it on a ready platform


**Fits your process** ⚠️ Only if your process matches the template ✅ Built exactly as described ✅ Built around how your team and clients actually work


**Logins, hosting and security** ✅ Handled by the vendor ⚠️ Yours to set up and maintain ✅ Handled by the platform


**Control over who sees what** ⚠️ Preset roles, often per client folder ⚠️ Lives in the code, so someone technical has to check it ✅[Permission rules](https://noloco.io/product/permissions) you can see, test and change without code


**Who can change it later** The vendor decides what changes Someone who can read the code, or re-prompting that can break what already works Your own team, by asking Nola or editing directly


**Branding** ⚠️ Custom domain and removing vendor branding often on higher plans ✅ Fully yours ✅ Custom domain, logo and colors


**Uses the data you already have** ⚠️ Usually means importing or duplicating data ✅ If the connection is built and maintained ✅[Airtable](https://noloco.io/data/airtable) , Google Sheets, PostgreSQL or[Noloco Tables](https://noloco.io/data/noloco-tables)


**Work behind the portal** ⚠️ Often tracked in a separate tool ✅ If built ✅ Team views and[workflows](https://noloco.io/product/workflows) on the same data clients see


**Ongoing cost** Subscription, often priced per client or seat Developer time or AI tool fees, plus hosting and fixes Subscription, see[current pricing](https://noloco.io/pricing)


Off-the-shelf makes sense when your process is standard and you mainly need file sharing and messaging. Custom code makes sense when you have someone technical to own it long term. **An AI portal builder fits when your process has exceptions, changes often, and the person who runs the operation needs to change the portal without breaking what already works.**


For client portals, the permissions question decides it. A mistake there means one client sees another client's data. Whichever route you choose, make sure you can see and test who has access to what before any client logs in.

## How do you build a white label client portal with Noloco?


1. **Connect your data.** Point Noloco at your existing Airtable base, spreadsheet, or database, or start fresh with Noloco's own database if you don't have one yet.
2. **Build the client views.** Use the AI builder to lay out what a client sees when they log in: status, files, reports, whatever's relevant to them.
3. **Set permissions before you set branding.** Decide who sees what, staff, contractors, and each client group, before you spend time on how it looks.
4. **Add your branding.** Logo, colors, and a custom domain, so nothing points back to Noloco.
5. **Automate the repetitive parts.** Set up workflows for onboarding steps, approval notifications, or status updates you're currently sending manually.
6. **Test with one real client before rolling out to everyone.** Confirm their permission level and their view actually work before it's live for your whole client base.

## Final thoughts


A white label client portal isn't really about the branding, that's just the visible part. What it actually does is move client coordination out of email and into one place both sides can check, which is where the real time and cost savings come from.


Assembly, Softr, Zite, and SuiteDash each solve a piece of that differently, built-in workflow, fast building on existing data, AI-generated first drafts, or an all-in-one suite. Before choosing, check all three jobs: **how far the branding goes on the plan you'll actually pay for, how precisely you can control what each client sees, and whether your team can run the work behind the portal in the same system.**

## FAQ


### What is a **white label client portal** ?


A white-label client portal is a secure online space, branded as your own, where clients log in to see the files, updates, reports, or tasks relevant to them, instead of chasing that information across email and other tool.


### **How do I choose a white label client portal platform?**


**‍** Check whether it connects to data you already have, controls access by client, matches your actual process, lets you brand the full experience, and doesn't require a developer for routine changes. Pricing that scales sensibly as you add clients matters too.


### **Is a white label client portal secure?** ‍


It should support[role-based permissions](https://guides.noloco.io/users-and-permissions/user-roles-and-permissions) so clients only see their own data, single sign-on rather than password-only login, and audit logs showing who accessed what. Ask any platform you're evaluating to confirm these directly rather than assuming.


### **How much does a white label client portal cost?**


**‍** It varies widely by platform and by how many clients you're giving access to. White-label features, such as a custom domain and removing the vendor's branding, are often only on paid or higher plans. Compare the cost at the number of clients you expect to have in a year, not just today.


Noloco's Free plan supports unlimited team seats and 50 client seats at no cost; the Build plan starts at $79 a month for 10 team seats and 1,000 client seats ([Noloco pricing](https://noloco.io/pricing) , October 2026).


### **Can you build a white label client portal with AI?**


Yes, and there are two ways to do it. AI coding tools generate an app's code from a prompt, which you then host, secure, and maintain yourself. AI portal builders use AI to set up the portal on a platform that already handles logins, permissions, hosting, and branding. For a portal that clients will use, the key check is the same either way: can you see and test exactly what each client has access to, without reading code?


### **How long does it take to launch a white label client portal?**


**‍** A simple portal with one or two client views can go live in a day or two. One with detailed permissions, multiple client types, and workflow automation takes longer, budget for testing with a real client before rolling it out to everyone.

- **Cost-effective** — No need for a dev team; Noloco handles hosting, updates, and security.
- **Custom branding** — Use your own domain, logo, and colors.
- **Feature-rich** — Secure login, databases, workflows, file sharing, dashboards, and more.
- **Client-first UX** — Noloco portals are built to look and feel like a natural extension of your brand.
